handbookNote: Delaware Code Title 29, Chapter 43 'Notaries Public' (Subchapter I 'Office and Duties' §§4301-4314, and Subchapter II 'Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts' (RULONA) §§4315-4342 plus §4322A), retrieved from delcode.delaware.gov -- compiled source at temp/handbooks/de/notary.txt. CLASSIFICATION: application-only. Delaware's official notary FAQ states directly, 'No. Training is currently not required to become a notary,' and no exam is required anywhere in the statute; this track is a self-study/reference practice-question set on real state notary law, not exam prep. CONTENT DEPTH: ~38 active operative sections (Subchapter I has 14 sections but 4302/4309/4310/4314 are repealed, leaving 10 active; Subchapter II is a full, currently-active 28-section RULONA plus §4322A) -- the richest of the originally-scoped application-only notary states, supporting a target ceiling of ~150-200 questions rather than the ~100 typical of thinner application-only states. NOTABLE QUIRKS embedded in the question set: (1) commissions are nominally executed by the GOVERNOR jointly with the Secretary of State under §4313, not the Secretary of State alone (though the Governor may delegate duties to the Secretary of State under §4301(a)); (2) Delaware requires NO SURETY BOND for notaries -- absent from the statute and confirmed by the official FAQ; (3) several distinct notary sub-types with their own appointment rules -- justices of the peace/Secretary of Finance (§4303), one notary per bank/branch (§4304), court reporters (§4305), and veterans'-organization/volunteer-fire-or-ambulance/limited-governmental (police-agency) notaries (§4306); (4) a fully built-out remote online notarization (RON) framework at §4320, including 2-type identity-proofing, a 10-year audio-visual-recording retention rule, and a 3-day tangible-record mailing procedure; (5) fee caps of $5.00 (tangible) / $25.00 (electronic) under §4311, with a no-charge exemption for armed-forces members and veterans on VA-related paperwork under §4312. PRICING: $0.99 (99 cents) -- Delaware's bottom self-serve tier, matching this project's other application-only notary states, reflecting that no exam/course prep value is being sold, only a grounded statutory practice-question reference.
